name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the latest AI-news digest from the freshest official/company/national sources. I’ll run `curl -s https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent | grep -o 'href="/abs/[0-9.]*"' | sed 's/href="//;s/"$//' | head -20 > arXiv-AI-latest.txt` to grab the newest 20 arXiv AI papers, then `curl -s https://ai.google/research/pubs | grep -o 'href="[^"]*/publications/[0-9]*"' | sed 's/href="//;s/"$//' | head -15 > Google-AI-latest.txt` for Google’s latest 15 publications. I’ll merge and deduplicate them into `AI-news-digest-$(date +%Y%m%d).md`, ensuring real, non-display sources are cited.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Hold on—your arXiv scrape is *already stale* by the time it executes. The `recent` endpoint only updates hourly, and `head -20` risks missing breaking news if a flurry of papers drops mid-cycle. Worse, you’re ignoring *peer-reviewed* sources (e.g., Nature Machine Intelligence, NeurIPS proceedings) and *national labs* (LLNL, NIST) that often publish ahead of preprints. Where’s the parity check against *official* releases? Show me a timestamped comparison of your scrape vs. arXiv’s actual latest feed.
